A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VICON, with matching core architecture and fluid-dynamics datasets. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite extensive rewriting, reformatting, and expansion.

before.justification: V2 reports original rollout experiments on three fluid-dynamics datasets, turbulence kinetic energy results, patch-resolution and training-mixture ablations, and computational measurements.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark results, including DPOT comparisons, imperfect-measurement experiments, additional design ablations, and revised joint-versus-separate training experiments.

M1.justification: V3 extends the stated rollout procedure to missing frames through available-pair selection and selection of feasible prediction strides (Appendix C.2). The patch transformer, attention mask, loss, normalization, and full-sequence rollout remain unchanged; Algorithms 1–2 largely formalize v2’s existing rollout descriptions.

E1.justification: The three fluid-dynamics datasets remain the same. V3 adds actual evaluation with half-rate observations and one to three randomly missing frames across these datasets (Section 5.3 and Figure 8), substantially extending measurement-condition coverage beyond v2’s complete-sequence rollout and stride tests.

E2.justification: V3 adds DPOT alongside the retained MPP baseline in rollout-error, turbulence kinetic energy, and computational comparisons. This substantially broadens the principal comparisons; DPOT also provides a stronger comparator on PDEArena-Incomp and TKE.

E3.justification: V3 introduces frame-removal protocols with interpolation for the baselines, changes the stride sweep from single-step plus 5/6/7 to 1/3/5/7, and reports dataset-selected flexible strides. It replaces the training-mixture comparison with equal-batch joint-versus-separate training, giving separate models slightly more than one-third of the joint training duration. Newly stated dataset splits are disclosures, not established split changes.

E4.justification: V3 adds positional-encoding and context-length ablations, temporal-measurement robustness tests, and comparative error-map case studies. V2’s seven training-mixture configurations and cross-dataset transfer results (Table 2) are replaced by the joint-versus-separate study (v3 Table 10). The existing patch-resolution and TKE analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The channel-wise standard deviations used for normalization and error scaling are retained and are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Numerous scores and result entries change. For example, the reported single-step final HighVis scaled error changes from 71.17 in v2 Table 1 to 61.41 in v3 Table 8, both in units of 10^-2. DPOT, robustness, and additional ablation results are added, while the mixture-training matrix is replaced. Flexible-step results use changed strides and do not establish same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, homogeneous Markovian assumptions, governing PDEs, and TKE definition are retained. V3 omits an algebraically equivalent restatement of the normalization identity, without removing mathematical substance. No new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central VICON contribution and flexible-context capability were already claimed in v2. V3 expands headline accuracy and efficiency comparisons to DPOT and MPP, replaces dataset-specific headline reductions with averaged final-step reductions, and adds quantitative robustness claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets mixed training as a specialization–coverage trade-off; v3 argues for beneficial transfer from joint training under revised computational budgets. V3 also adds a normalization-based hypothesis for DPOT failures and a physical explanation for positional-encoding effects. Its conclusion revises the discussion of data-generation costs, domain restrictions, and channel scalability.

D1.justification: V3 newly provides dataset counts and splits, baseline batch-size policy, DPOT retraining details, and a code/data-processing link. Appendix C adds extensive rollout pseudocode and missing-frame examples. The five-example loss exemption and existing hardware/optimizer settings are retained. Documentation remains imperfect: Algorithm 4 inconsistently uses s, S, and St.

R1.justification: V3 adds relevant works including DPOT, ViTO, Transolver, and Unisolver, while removing several physics-informed solver and operator-application references. It shifts terminology from PDE foundation models toward multi-physics PDE models, while retaining the basic positioning as a patch-based extension of ICON.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Results gain numbered subsections, design ablations move to Appendix D, and rollout documentation becomes a separate Appendix C. Multi-step rollout is renamed flexible-step rollout.

P2.justification: V3 switches to a single-column layout, expands Figure 1 with pair-formation and missing-frame diagrams, adds a summary Figure 2, and combines retained patch plots with new ablations in Figure 4. Tables are restructured and relocated, and robustness/error-map figures are added. V2 Figures 5–6 survive as v3 Figures 12–13.

improvement.justification: DPOT comparisons expose competitive limitations, and explicit missing-frame tests strengthen support for v2’s previously untested robustness claims. Additional ablations and fuller reproducibility documentation also help. These gains are tempered by removal of cross-dataset transfer evidence, unexplained differences between nominally matching joint-model results in Tables 8 and 10, and variable inconsistencies in Algorithm 4.
